faq.q: Where do new skin cells come from?
faq.a: New skin cells are made in the basal layer at the bottom of the epidermis, where stem cells divide constantly. The new cells are pushed up towards the surface.

faq.q: How many skin cells do we shed?
faq.a: We shed tens of thousands of dead skin cells every minute, roughly 30,000 to 40,000, which adds up to millions every day.
asks: How much skin do we lose a day?
Do we shed skin all the time?

faq.q: How often does skin replace itself?
faq.a: The epidermis renews itself about every four weeks in young adults, as cells travel up from the basal layer and flake off. It slows down with age.
asks: How long does skin take to renew?
Do we get new skin every month?

faq.q: Why are the top skin cells dead?
faq.a: As skin cells rise they fill with keratin and lose their nucleus, becoming flat, tough, dead scales. This dead layer is waterproof and protects the living cells beneath.
asks: Is the outside of skin alive?

faq.q: Is house dust made of dead skin?
faq.a: Dead skin cells are part of house dust, but studies show much of it also comes from outdoor soil, fibres from clothes and furniture, pollen and other particles.

facts: The human epidermis renews itself roughly every four weeks.
People shed roughly 30,000 to 40,000 dead skin cells every minute.

quiz.say: Where in the skin are new skin cells made?
quiz.show: New skin cells are made in…

options.show: The basal layer at the bottom of the epidermis
options.say: The basal layer at the bottom of the epidermis

quiz.why: Stem cells in the basal layer divide constantly, and their daughter cells move up to the surface.

wrong.1: The surface cells are dead and simply flake off.
wrong.2: Hair is made by follicles, not the source of new skin cells.
